summary.en: Model item prefixes and capacities, recover whole-item choices, and compress space without reusing an item.
summary.bn: item ও capacity দিয়ে state বানাও, নেওয়া জিনিস বের করো এবং একই জিনিস দুবার না নিয়ে space কমাও।

practice.title: Choose indivisible equipment
practice.statementHtml: Read n (0..12), capacity (0..20), then weight value pairs (weight 1..20, value 0..99). Print Enter n capacity and weight value pairs: first, then value = V.
hints: Both recurrence branches must read the previous item row.

practice.title: List the optimal equipment IDs
practice.statementHtml: Use the same knapsack input format and bounds. Print Enter n capacity and weight value pairs:, then value = V and chosen: followed by increasing zero-based IDs. Skip the later item on a tied value.
hints: A row value equal to the value above it means the item may be skipped.

practice.title: 0/1 Knapsack: justify the decisions
practice.statementHtml: Explain why the recurrence or decision rule for 0/1 Knapsack covers every valid candidate, and why evaluation terminates.
hints: A 0/1 item can be selected at most once.
practice.answerHtml:
Every feasible subset from the first i items either excludes item i-1 or includes it. Excluding it leaves a feasible subset from the first i-1 items at capacity c. Including it leaves capacity c-weight[i-1] and forbids using that same item again. The previous-row optimum therefore gives the best possible value in each case.

The recurrence takes the larger value among these exhaustive, feasible cases. An empty item prefix has optimum zero. Induction on i proves each row, regardless of whether the bag uses every unit of capacity. This is an at-most-capacity argument; exact-fill knapsack would require unreachable states and a different base treatment.

Reconstruction follows a branch that attains the stored value. A changed row value must have come from taking the item, because skipping would copy the previous row. An unchanged value can be attained by skipping, even if taking also ties. The row always decreases, so recovery stops after at most n decisions and never repeats an item.

practice.title: 0/1 Knapsack: derive resource bounds
practice.statementHtml: Derive the time and auxiliary-space bounds for the implementations of 0/1 Knapsack. Separate input, working storage and returned information.
hints: A compact value row alone loses straightforward reconstruction.
practice.answerHtml:
There are (n+1)(C+1) states and constant work per state. Time and table storage are Θ(nC) for positive variable n and C, with boundary dimensions included when either is zero. Reconstruction takes O(n) time and at most O(n) output space for chosen IDs. Fixed demonstration bounds do not turn the general algorithm into constant time.

Capacity is a numeric magnitude rather than its number of input bits. Consequently the bound is pseudo-polynomial. A huge capacity can make this table impractical even when n is moderate. Other approaches may use value-indexed DP, meet-in-the-middle search, or a different formulation depending on constraints.

The exercises permit at most twelve items, capacity twenty, and values at most 99. The largest possible value is at most 1188, so int is sufficient. Positive weights prevent a free repeated-use ambiguity, though zero-weight 0/1 items could be handled with a carefully stated model. They are excluded here to keep the contract consistent.

practice.title: 0/1 Knapsack: explain the worked trace
practice.statementHtml: Reproduce the worked 0/1 Knapsack trace and explain each comparison or state change. State how the example handles equal candidates.
hints: Name the quantities in each row before making the next decision.
practice.answerHtml:
Items availablec=012345

items 0..1004559

Items availablec=012345
none000000
item 0004444
items 0..1004559
items 0..2004579

At the final capacity 5, row three equals row two, so skip item 2. Row two at capacity 5 differs from row one, so take item 1 and move to capacity 2. Row one at 2 differs from row zero, so take item 0. Their weights sum to 5 and values sum to 9.

quiz.prompt: What does dp[i][c] mean in this 0/1 table?
options: Best value from the first i items within capacity c
Number of copies of item i
quiz.explanation: The state limits item availability and imposes an upper capacity bound.

quiz.prompt: Which row supplies the take predecessor?
quiz.explanation: Reading the previous item row prevents taking the current item again.

quiz.prompt: Which capacity direction preserves 0/1 use in one row?
quiz.explanation: Smaller source capacities must still belong to the previous item stage.

quiz.prompt: For a tied row value during recovery, what does this lesson do?
quiz.explanation: The previous row already attains the same optimum.

quiz.prompt: Can unused capacity remain in the optimal answer?
options: Yes, capacity is an upper bound
No, every unit must be filled
Only if an item is split
quiz.explanation: The empty subset and other underfilled subsets remain feasible.

quiz.prompt: What additional information does simple recovery need beyond one overwritten value row?
options: Earlier rows or justified saved decisions
quiz.explanation: The one-row optimum alone no longer exposes each earlier item's branch.

quiz.prompt: Why can ratio-first fail for whole equipment items?
options: The ratios are undefined for positive weights
All whole items must be taken
Remaining capacity may not fit the needed combination
quiz.explanation: Divisibility was essential to fractional knapsack's equal-weight exchange.

quiz.prompt: What value does one weight-two item earn at capacity four in compact 0/1 DP?
quiz.explanation: Descending updates allow the single item only once.

quiz.prompt: What value can capacity five obtain from weights two,three,four?
quiz.explanation: The first two items fit together and earn nine.

quiz.prompt: What value remains possible at zero capacity with positive weights?
quiz.explanation: No item fits, so empty selection retains zero.

keyPoints.bn: ০/১ সমস্যায় একটি জিনিস সর্বোচ্চ একবার নেওয়া যায়।

keyPoints.en: Both branches read the previous item row.
keyPoints.bn: নেওয়া ও বাদ দেওয়া দুই ক্ষেত্রেই আগের item-এর সারি লাগে।

keyPoints.en: Equal row values allow skipping the later item.
keyPoints.bn: আগের সারির মান সমান হলে পরের জিনিসটি বাদ দেওয়া যায়।

keyPoints.en: Descending compact capacities prevent current-item reuse.
keyPoints.bn: capacity কমতে থাকলে চলতি জিনিস আবার নেওয়া হয় না।

keyPoints.en: A compact value row alone loses straightforward reconstruction.
keyPoints.bn: শুধু ছোট value row রাখলে সরাসরি choice ফেরত পাওয়া যায় না।
